Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our conversation I attached a compact pricing spreadsheet (HA_Pack_Pricing_v2.xlsx) showing three ways to buy High-Availability (HA) coverage on top of your existing Dedicated deployment:

- Modular HA add-on (consumption + per-incident credits): pay-as-you-go for failover activations and cross-region traffic spikes.
- Retainer overlay (monthly): flat monthly fee that pre-purchases a pool of rapid-response hours and incident credits.
- Hybrid commit: annual commit for baseline credits + lower per-incident pricing for overages.

Key differentiators we discussed: automated prefix/KV cache replication for warm failover, 5ms average extra latency in cross-region failover tests, and the ability to map specific runbook escalation tiers to your SRE roster (we can assign named on-call handoffs).

Please review the attachment; noted columns: uptime band (99.9/99.95/99.99), target triage response (15/5/1 hours), escalation coverage (L1/L2/x-on-call), and suggested volume break discounts at 500k/2M token-months.

Two asks: can you confirm whether Procurement prefers a retainer PO or a consumption-based PO for pilots, and would you like a short call tomorrow to walk the numbers?

Thanks,

Elena —

Quick answers inline and a suggested configuration based on your load profile: 

1) Credit rollover: For pilots we allow a 30-day rollover bucket for unused incident credits (one-time exception). For annual Hybrid commits, unused credits can roll quarterly (subject to contract language).

2) Response SLA start: times measured from our ingest (receipt) timestamp in the routing layer. We can instrument a PagerDuty acknowledgement hook to align metrics, but legal SLA language must reference our server receipt time. Practically, that maps closely to your alerts if PD is integrated.

3) Volume discount: We can offer an 8% discount on the retainer line at 2.4M token-months (instead of 10%). For an additional 1% discount we can require a 12-month prepay vs monthly billing.

Suggested pilot configuration (30 days):
- Hybrid pilot: $12,500 monthly retainer (includes 100 incident credits + 40 rapid-response hours), 20% reduced per-incident rate for overages.
- Add-on features: warm KV cache replication (enabled), cross-region failover testing (one scheduled test included).
- Escalation: L1 (triage) -> L2 (eng escalation) -> Customer SRE on-call; named escalation contacts required.

I've attached a condensed runbook sample (redwood-runbook-sample.pdf) showing handoff windows; we can scope the 02:00–06:00 PT shadowing to the first 30 days.

If Procurement prefers PO for retainer pilots, we can issue a template with payment terms Net 30 and an option for a prepay discount.

—Ben

Read the thread. A couple of internal notes for alignment before we send Procurement the PO template: 

- Discount authority: Sales may approve up to 10% on the retainer line for deals < $200k ARR; anything above requires Finance sign-off. Jordan, this deal appears sub-$200k on first-year ARR with the hybrid pilot, so you can confirm final discounting with Ben.
- Billing cadence: Procurement prefers a PO for monthly retainer pilots. We should offer both monthly invoicing and an optional 12-month prepay with a 1% additional discount.
- SLA measurement clause: Legal will reference our server receipt timestamp as Ben noted. Add a clause for paired instrumentation (PagerDuty hook) and a BI report for monthly SLA attainment so StarkBank can reconcile credits.
- Termination and credits: Include a 30-day termination escape during the pilot with pro-rated refunds for prepay; incident credits are non-refundable but may be transferred to a new contract within 60 days if both parties agree.

I've prepared a PO template and a standard addendum that includes runbook obligations and named escalation contacts. Laura, please attach the PO template to the HubSpot deal and push DocuSign for signature when Jordan confirms.
